thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts for private-gateway-prod. 5xx-rate=18% over baseline, 504/timeouts spike, source=egress/transit appliance. Paging @oncall-john and networking oncall.

John H: saw the page, jumping in. Which customers are hitting this?

Liz O: fintech-client-prod and ml-ops-team-prod see the highest error rates — they're coming from our Private/VPC transit path to the inference gateway. Errors are 502/504, some 500.

Miguel R: grabbing metrics. NAT gateway ephemeral port usage is high, conntrack is approaching quota on the transit appliance. Also seeing asymmetric flows where replies are coming back via a different path and being dropped.

Alex P: logs from the gateway show repeated "upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream" and NLB 504s. I pasted a snippet:
```
2026-03-14T02:10:12Z gateway nginx[2132]: 504 upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream, client=10.12.34.56
2026-03-14T02:10:13Z nat-appliance kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```

Evan S: can you run conntrack count? Miguel, any recent SG or peering changes?

Miguel R: running remote: `ssh infra-transit-02 'sudo conntrack -C'` -> returns 65534 (limit 65536). Also saw a peering flapping event in the route table at 01:48 UTC — that created asymmetric SNAT.

John H: immediate impact: multi-tenant private inference requests are failing intermittently. CS reported degraded production inference for fintech-client-prod. Is there a quick mitigation?

Liz O: mitigation options: scale NAT/replace transit appliance, clear conntrack entries for affected subnets, temporarily route affected customers to hosted fallback, or add a short-term increase to conntrack size (requires careful kernel param change and restart).

Miguel R: I've cleared conntrack entries for the fintech-client-prod subnet to reclaim ephemeral ports: `sudo conntrack -D -s 10.12.34.0/24` — freed ~12k entries. Error rate dropped a bit.

John H: good. Can we push a routing fallback so that fintech-client-prod traffic goes to hosted inference pool for 1 hour? That will reduce customer impact.

Alex P: started canary reroute: updating the smart-routing policy for tenant-fintech to prefer hosted-api with lower priority to private when failures > 5%. Patch applied via console, pushing now.

incident-bot: @John H update: routing change applied to 12% of traffic for tenant-fintech as canary.

CSM Sam: notified fintech client that we're investigating and routing a portion of their traffic to a hosted fallback to reduce errors. "No data lost; some requests may go to hosted models." They asked for ETA.

Evan S: we should also check recent infra deploys — any kernel/security group changes?

Miguel R: looked at recent commits — no SG changes, but a peering retransmit event coincided with a failed BGP update from partner region (logs attached). That caused asymmetric NAT: return traffic hitting different NAT appliance which didn't have conntrack entry -> 5xx/504.

John H: action list for now:
- Miguel: continue cleaning conntrack and monitor ephemeral port utilization (in progress).
- Alex: keep canary ramp until errors <2% for fintech.
- Liz: coordinate with infra to spin up replacement transit appliance and failover the peering (ETA 25m).
- Evan: check kernel tunes for nf_conntrack and whether we can safely bump hashsize without reboot.
- CS: keep the customer updated every 15m.

Miguel R: spun up transit-03 and began sync of NAT state. Prep to cut peering to transit-02 and switch traffic. Running `ip route`/`iptables -t nat -L -n` checks.

Alex P: canary ramp to 40% now. Error rates for fintech down from 30% -> 6% after conntrack clear + canary. Still seeing occasional 504s for other tenants.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Pager acknowledged by John H, incident severity = P1. Handoff to networking for mitigation.

Liz O: infra will do a failover to transit-03 in ~10m. Miguel, coordinate the cut and watch for conntrack re-population. Also create a temporary sticky SNAT rule so replies return to the same appliance.

Miguel R: cut executed at 02:33 UTC. Transit-03 is answering SNAT. Observed a short spike but then 5xx count trended down. Conntrack count stable ~22k.

John H: customer update posted: "We identified root cause as transient peering flap that led to asymmetric SNAT and conntrack exhaustion on our transit appliance. We routed your traffic to our hosted fallback and cut over to a fresh transit appliance. Errors are decreasing; we expect full recovery in <30m. We'll follow up with RCA."

CSM Sam: fintech acknowledged, appreciates the proactive reroute. They asked for permanent mitigations.

Evan S: long-term fixes proposed in-thread: add automated conntrack trimming for idle flows, increase nf_conntrack table size on transit appliances, implement sticky SNAT for private peers, and add peering BGP health checks to auto-failover before asymmetry.

Alex P: will open a postmortem ticket and link this thread. Root cause preliminary: peering BGP flap -> asymmetric SNAT -> conntrack table exhaustion -> gateway 504s.

John H: handing off to Miguel R for network ops follow-up and RCA write-up. I'll continue to monitor and escalate if needed.

Miguel R: taking ownership. Current status: mitigation in place, error rates trending down to baseline. Next update in 20m, will post RCA timeline and patch plan.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Closed for page handoff.

(threads and logs attached by Alex P and Miguel R in channel files)
